questions.question: All Indian Muslim league was formed at Dacca in _________.
questions.solution: 1906 was the year the All-India Muslim League was formed in Dacca. Founders: Aga Khan III and Nawab Salimullah.

questions.question: Kitab ul-Hind an Arabic text was written by ________.
questions.solution: Al-Biruni wrote the Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic. History: He accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India and studied Indian culture and science.

questions.question:
The rules made for the Buddhist “Sangha” were written down in a book called ________.
(d) Vinaya pitaka
(b) Sutta pitaka
(c) Milinda Panha
(d) Abhidhammapitaka
Ans: a

Q175. Who occupied Badaun (A.D. 1197-98) and appointed Iltutmish as its first Muslim Governor?
questions.solution: Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules for the Buddhist Sangha. Qutbuddin Aibak was the one who occupied Badaun and appointed Iltutmish as Governor. Note: The question includes two parts in the text.

questions.question: Who among the following was a Shaka ruler in India (AD 130-150)?
questions.solution: Rudradaman I was the most famous Shaka ruler. Legacy: Famous for the Junagadh rock inscription (written in chaste Sanskrit) and repairing the Sudarshana Lake.

questions.question: Which among the following was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan?
questions.solution: <u>Aurangzeb</u> was the son of Shahjahan who emerged victorious in the war of succession against his brothers Dara Shikoh, Shuja, and Murad.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was overthrown by British and sent to exile in Burma, after the revolt of 1857?
questions.solution: Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) was the last Mughal emperor. He was tried for treason after the 1857 revolt and exiled to Rangoon (Burma).

questions.question: The sepoys of Meerut arrived at the Gates of Red Fort to meet the Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah on _____.
questions.solution: <u>11 May, 1857</u> is when the sepoys reached Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as the Emperor of Hindustan. The revolt began on 10 May in Meerut.

questions.question: Who was the last tirthankara of the Jainas?
questions.solution: Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism. Info: He was born at Kundagrama and attained Kaivalya.

questions.question: Alluri Sitaram Raju was a tribal freedom fighter from state ________ of India.
questions.solution: Andhra Pradesh was the base for Alluri Sitaram Raju, who led the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) against the British forest laws.

questions.question: The British parliament transferred the powers of east India company to the British crown in _______.
questions.solution: 1858 (Government of India Act 1858) was when the East India Company's rule ended and the administration was taken over by the British Crown.

questions.question: In India, the practice of erecting megaliths began about ________ ago.
questions.solution: 3000 years ago marked the beginning of megalith (large stone) construction in India, especially in the Deccan and South India.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at ________.
questions.solution: Bodh gaya (Bihar) is where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree and became the 'Buddha'.

questions.question: Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?
questions.solution: Indus valley civilization (Harappan Civilization) is renowned for its grid-pattern town planning and advanced drainage systems.

questions.question: Who were the prime accused in the Assembly bomb case that took place in 1929, Delhi?
questions.solution: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929 to protest against the Public Safety Bill and Trade Dispute Bill.

questions.question: When did the Chauri Chaura incident take place?
questions.solution: <u>1922</u> (February 4) was when the Chauri Chaura incident occurred in Gorakhpur district, prompting Gandhi to halt the Non-Cooperation movement.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters gave the famous quote “Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!”?
questions.solution: Subhash Chandra Bose gave the slogan 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!' to motivate the Indian National Army (INA).

questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai was an active member of which organisation?
questions.solution: Arya Samaj (founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati) had Lala Lajpat Rai as a prominent leader. He also founded the Punjab National Bank.

questions.question: In the mid-eighth century, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed a ritual literally called a _______.
questions.solution: Golden womb (Hiranya-garbha) was the ritual performed by Dantidurga to acquire the status of a Kshatriya after overthrowing the Chalukyas.

questions.question: Which of the following has founded the city of Jaipur?
questions.solution: Sawai Jai Singh II founded the city of Jaipur in 1727. Scientific contribution: He built five astronomical observatories called Jantar Mantar.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks?
questions.solution: Bindusara was referred to as Amitrochates (derived from Sanskrit Amitraghata) by Greek writers like Athenaeus.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots of 1875 took place in __________.
questions.solution: Maharashtra (specifically Pune and Ahmednagar) was the center of the 1875 Deccan Riots. Reason: Peasant uprising against the heavy interest of moneylenders.

questions.question: Which act of British Parliament was also known as East India Company Act 1793?
questions.solution: <u>The Charter Act, 1793</u> is the correct name. It renewed the Company's commercial privileges for another 20 years.

questions.question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
questions.solution: <u>Regulating Act</u> of 1773 was the first step taken by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.

questions.question: Kalinga that was conquered by Ashoka is the ancient name of _______.
questions.solution: Coastal Orissa is the region known as Kalinga in ancient times. The Kalinga War (261 BC) was the turning point in Ashoka's life.

questions.question: Editor of a Marathi newspaper “Kesari” was _______.
questions.solution: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the editor of Kesari (Marathi) and The Mahratta (English).
